shorts.title: Christmas Hearts: which three would you pass?
shorts.question:
Which three
would you pass?
shorts.context: A Hearts hand for your Christmas table.
shorts.questionBottom:
The queen of spades costs 13 points.
Each heart costs one.
shorts.selectionBottom:
Get rid of the queen
and your two highest spades.
shorts.answerTitle:
No small spades
to hide behind.
shorts.answerBottom:
Keeping K♠ or A♠ could mean
winning the queen later.

caveat.heading:
But look at
those hearts.
caveat.context: K♥ and A♥ are still dangerous.
caveat.explanation:
Passing spades does not solve everything.
Reconsider after receiving your cards.

discussion.heading:
What would your
family pass?
discussion.context: The same hand can start a debate.
discussion.question:
Spades, hearts, or a mix?
Tell us your three cards and why.

shorts.caption: A Hearts dilemma for the Christmas card table: which three would you pass? The high spades are dangerous, but so are the high hearts. There is a reason for this choice, not a rule to always pass Q♠ K♠ A♠. What would your family do? Actual lesson cards from Barbu. #Hearts #CardGames #Christmas
shorts.conversationPrompt: Which three would you pass, and why? Would anyone at your Christmas table disagree?

shorts.title: Christmas Gin Rummy: would you discard this king?
shorts.question:
One card must go.
Which one?
shorts.context: A Gin Rummy hand for two this Christmas.
shorts.questionBottom:
Keep your sets and runs.
Unmatched cards count against you.
shorts.selectionContext: The king is outside your combinations.
shorts.selectionBottom:
Keep the three sevens
and both complete runs.
shorts.answerBottom:
Deadwood is the value
of cards outside your sets and runs.

caveat.heading:
But watch your
opponent too.
caveat.context: If you keep playing, they can take it.
caveat.explanation:
You could knock on two deadwood.
If you play on, watch their pickups.

discussion.heading:
Would you still
throw the king?
discussion.context: If you play on: suppose they took Q♠.
discussion.question:
Does that change your choice?
What would you watch for?

shorts.caption: A two-player Christmas card-table dilemma: which card would you discard in Gin Rummy? Two deadwood points let you knock. If you choose to keep playing instead, consider a hypothetical twist: what if your opponent just picked up Q♠? Would you change your discard? Actual lesson cards from Barbu; the opponent pickup is a discussion scenario, not a recorded move. #GinRummy #CardGames #Christmas
shorts.conversationPrompt: Would you knock on two deadwood or play on? If you play on, would an opponent picking up Q♠ change your discard?
